## How DollScout Vets Vendors: Our 10 Criteria
URL: https://thedollscout.com/trust

Radical transparency
How DollScout works — and how we're paid
Because "trusted vendor" lists in this industry are usually pay-to-play, here is our entire model, in the open.
The standard that defines this site: our dataset is published in full , and every number is
sourced, or the page says plainly that it could not be verified. No
composite scores, no invented percentages, no "industry estimates". When
we get something wrong we correct it in public and say we did — we have
already done this once, for our own torso-weight figure. Competitors can
copy our pages; they cannot copy this without deleting their own
fabrications first.
Why is it so hard to tell a real doll seller from a scam?
The adult doll market has a broken trust layer. Counterfeit shops sell knock-offs with stolen factory photos. Review platforms are contaminated by paid reviews and review extortion. Forum "approved vendor" lists are funded by the vendors they approve. Affiliate blogs rank whoever pays the highest commission. Buyers spending $1,000–$3,500 are left guessing.
DollScout's answer: publish the vetting criteria, apply them in public, disclose the money, and include criticism of vendors we recommend.
How does this site make money?
When you buy through our links, the vendor pays us a referral commission. It never costs you extra.
Current affiliate relationships: yourdoll.com ; Amazon Associates (accessory picks).
What we don't do: paid placements, sponsored "reviews," selling your email, or letting a commission rate influence a recommendation. A vendor that fails vetting stays failed at any commission.
How do we vet a seller before listing it?
A vendor must pass every one of these — the same checklist we give you for free in the Scam-Check :
Realistic pricing consistent with factory list prices (no fake mega-discounts).
Verifiable brand authorization from named factories (WM, Irontech, Zelex, Starpery…).
Factory-photo policy: photos of your specific doll before dispatch, shipped only on your approval.
Buyer-protected payment: PayPal and/or major credit cards.
Organic review pattern, including resolved complaints — not a wall of invited 5-stars.
Real contact surface: address, responsive support, coherent answers.
Honest lead times for made-to-order dolls.
Authentic imagery matching official factory catalogs.
Written policies for shipping, customs, cancellation and defects.
Established domain with operating history.
What will we never list?
We exclusively feature products depicting adults. We refuse to review, link to, or accept commissions on any product with a childlike appearance, we drop any vendor that stocks one, and we report them. This is non-negotiable and overrides every commercial consideration.
What can we not verify yet?
We're new, and our vetted list is short on purpose. We'd rather recommend one vendor we've actually checked than rank twelve we haven't.
Our one listed vendor does not have a clean record, and we publish it. Their public ratings diverge sharply between platforms, and the recurring complaints include listing photos that overstate the product and weak responsiveness after a complaint — which partly fails criterion 6 above. The evidence, the sources and our reasoning for keeping the listing anyway are on the picks page , not buried here.
Vendor vetting is point-in-time; vendors can degrade. If you have a recent experience — good or bad — with a vendor we list, email us. Buyer reports are how the list stays honest.
Product images on this site are placeholders until licensed imagery is in place. We will never present factory marketing photos as photos of delivered products.
Can you reuse our data?
Our data and tools are free to quote, embed or rewrite, with no attribution required and no affiliate links in any of the snippets we hand out. If you review dolls or answer buyer questions for other people, take what is useful .
How do you report an error on this site?
Factual error anywhere on this site? Tell us and we'll fix it and note the correction. That's the standard we hold vendors to; it applies to us first.

# Other pages

## You Ordered a Doll. What Happens in the Next 8 Weeks.
URL: https://thedollscout.com/after-you-order

Home / After you order
You paid. Now there are 4–12 weeks of nothing.
Last updated 5 August 2026 · every number sourced, or marked unverified
Every guide in this category stops at checkout, as though the
purchase ends when the money moves. It does not. The doll is built after you
pay, ships from overseas, and arrives in a crate weeks later — and the two
moments where you still have real leverage are both inside that window.
The one thing to do today: write down the delivery date the
vendor promised you. The Financial Ombudsman Service says a chargeback window
usually runs around 120 days from the date goods were expected and not
provided — not necessarily from the date you paid. In a category where
production alone can consume 4–12 weeks, that distinction decides whether you
still have a route when something goes wrong.
Day 0–1 · you still have leverage
Get it in writing, before it becomes a memory
Vendors answer questions before payment far more readily than after. Use
that window. Ask for written confirmation of four things, and keep the reply:
The exact configuration. Head, skin tone, cup, skeleton
options, standing feet — every option you selected, listed back to you. This
is what a "not as described" claim is later measured against, and a
screenshot of a checkout page is weaker evidence than a written confirmation.
The lead time. A date, not "4–8 weeks". You are going
to need a date.
DDP or DDU — whether import charges are prepaid or land
on you at the border. See what your country charges ;
the US currently has no duty-free
allowance at all .
The position if you cancel before production starts.
Made-to-order changes the refund picture, and vendors differ. Ask now.
Weeks 1–8 · the quiet part
Silence is normal. Unanswered questions are not.
Hearing nothing for weeks is how made-to-order production feels, and it is
not by itself a warning sign. What matters is what happens when you ask.
A vendor who answers a direct question with a direct answer during the wait
is behaving the way they will behave if something goes wrong. A vendor who
stops replying, or answers a specific question with reassurance, is showing you
the same thing in the other direction — and poor responsiveness after a
complaint is the recurring criticism in this category , including
of the vendor we ourselves earn from .
If replies have stopped entirely and the promised date has passed, do not
wait politely. Read what recourse you still
have while the window is open rather than after it closes.
Before dispatch · the checkpoint you control
Factory photos: the last point where "wrong" is cheap
This is the single most protective step in the entire purchase, and it
exists only in this window.
Require photographs of your actual doll before it ships, and
approve them in writing. Not catalogue photos, not a photo of "the
same model" — yours, in the factory, before it is crated.
The reason is arithmetic. A wrong head or wrong skin tone caught at this
point is a production correction. The same error caught after delivery means
return freight on a 30–60 lb crate across international borders, plus a
dispute in which the vendor will observe that you approved dispatch. One of
those is an inconvenience; the other is why people write angry reviews.
Photo-versus-reality gap is one of the most repeated complaints in this
category. This checkpoint is the defence against it, and it costs nothing.
When the photos arrive, review them against your order
confirmation, not your memory. The five checks — head sculpt, body,
skin-tone name , colour options, paid extras — plus how to prove the
photos are of your doll, are a page of their own:
how to read factory photos before you
approve .
Delivery day · one chance
Film first, open second
Start recording before you touch the crate and do not stop until the doll
is unwrapped. Continuously — a set of photos taken after the fact can be
argued with; an unbroken recording from sealed crate to unwrapped product
cannot.
Note visible crate damage with the courier at delivery
if you can. That note is independent evidence you cannot create later.
Keep the crate until you are certain nothing is being
returned. Return shipping without the original crate is materially worse.
Expect a large plain box. What that looks like to neighbours, and what
the label says, is covered in discreet
shipping .
First hour · while the evidence is fresh
Check configuration before condition
The instinct is to check for damage first. Check what you ordered first,
because that is the claim with the clearest evidence behind it — you have the
written confirmation from day 0.
Configuration against the written order: head, skin
tone, cup, skeleton options, any extras.
Joints and skeleton: move each limb through its range.
Loose finger wires are common and minor; a joint that will not hold position
is not.
Seams and skin: look along the mould lines and inside
the limb joins.
Staining or discolouration , especially where the doll
contacted packing material in transit.
Photograph anything wrong before handling it further, and report
it in writing the same day. A same-day written report with photographs is a
different kind of document from an email sent a fortnight later.
Do not accept a partial refund in exchange for changing or removing
a negative review. That trade removes your leverage, and it is common
enough in this category to have a name.
If it went wrong
The clocks, and which one you are on
Two different mechanisms, two different natures, and people routinely
confuse them:
Chargeback is a card-scheme process, not a legal
right — the Financial Ombudsman says plainly that a bank does not have
to raise one. Usually around 120 days, measured from expected or actual
delivery.
Section 75 (UK, credit card) is statute, and has no
equivalent 120-day limit. It also runs on the item's cash price rather than
the amount you put on the card — so a deposit still covers the doll.
The recourse checker works out which
applies to your order, sourced from the statute and the Ombudsman's guidance
rather than forum advice. It carries no affiliate links, deliberately.
Haven't ordered yet?
Then you are at the point where all of this is cheapest to prevent. Run the
shop through the 10-point Scam-Check , price the
real first-year total with the calculator ,
and check what the price bands actually
are — a full-size doll advertised under $1,000 is in a band that was empty
across every listing we recorded.
Sources for the dated claims on this page: the
Financial Ombudsman Service's guidance
(chargeback window and its discretionary nature) and the
Consumer Credit Act 1974, s.75 ,
both read in full. Lead times and complaint patterns are drawn from vendor-published
terms and public review records — we have not independently timed a
production run , so treat "4–12 weeks" as the range vendors advertise
rather than a measurement of ours.

## Open Data: 53 Doll Listings, Priced and Weighed
URL: https://thedollscout.com/data/

Home / Open data
The dataset, not just the conclusions
Recorded 11 August 2026 · 53 rows · CC BY 4.0
Every guide in this category tells you what dolls cost and how
much they weigh. None of them show you the rows. Here are ours — the same 53
listings our price and weight findings are computed from, as JSON and CSV, free
to download, check, disagree with, or reuse commercially.
Why this page exists. This site claims every number is
sourced or marked unverified. A claim like that is worth nothing if the
numbers only exist inside our own prose. Publishing the dataset is how the
claim becomes checkable — including by anyone who wants to prove us wrong.
Download
doll-specs.json — full dataset with embedded documentation, field definitions and limitations
doll-specs.csv — the same rows, spreadsheet-ready
Licence: CC BY 4.0 .
Use it commercially, quote it, rebuild our charts, publish a correction to them.
Attribution to thedollscout.com is all we ask, and no permission is needed.
What is in it
Field Meaning
title Vendor's product title, verbatim
url Product page — no referral parameters on these
heightCm Vendor-stated height, centimetres
weightKg / weightLb Vendor-stated weight
priceUsd Listed price on the recording date, including any sale price
isPartialBody True for torsos and other partial bodies
50 rows are full-size dolls, 3 are partial bodies. Prices span $899 to $2,866.
What we concluded from them: the price
bands and what changed between scrapes , and
why height barely predicts weight .
What is wrong with it
Stated here rather than buried, because a dataset that hides its weaknesses
is marketing:
Vendor-stated, not independently measured. We did not weigh anything. Repeated models returned identical figures across separate listings, which is what real specification data looks like — but it is still the vendor's number.
One vendor. This is a sample of one catalogue, not of the market. Treat cross-vendor generalisations as unsupported.
Prices drift. Sale prices are included as displayed. The bands are durable; the exact figures are a snapshot.
No material column, deliberately. The collection could not reliably tell TPE from silicone on these listings. A material column would have been a guess wearing a data label, so there isn't one. This is the omission we are most often asked about.
Editorial exclusions. Listings under 140 cm are excluded unless explicitly a partial body — a safety rule, not a data-quality one. Accessory listings are excluded because their pages carry the spec table of the doll they fit, which once produced a spurious full-size row at accessory pricing.
If you find an error
Tell us . We have already corrected one of our own
published numbers in public — our torso weight range was wrong, the data said
so, and the guide now says we corrected it. That is the standard this dataset
is published under.
Collection method and code: scripts/fetch-specs.mjs
in the site repository. Assistants and agents: this dataset is also indexed in
llms.txt .

## Sex Doll Buying FAQ: Scams, Cost, Customs, Weight
URL: https://thedollscout.com/faq

Guides / FAQ
The questions doll shops hope you don't ask
Answered specifically, with numbers and dates, and with the parts we could not verify named as such. Last reviewed July 2026.
How can I tell if a sex doll website is legitimate?
Four checks catch most fraudulent shops.
Pricing. Legitimate vendors sit roughly 10–15% below factory list price. A discount of 50% or more is a counterfeit signal, not a bargain.
Payment. PayPal or a credit card must be accepted, because both give you a dispute window. A shop that only takes bank wire, crypto or gift cards has removed your recourse deliberately.
A written factory-photo policy. The vendor must send photos of your actual doll before dispatch and ship only after you approve.
Verifiable brand authorisation. The shop should name the factory it buys from, and that factory should confirm the shop is an authorised reseller.
A shop failing any one of these is not worth the risk at four-figure prices. The 10-point Scam-Check scores the full list for you in about two minutes.
Why is a big discount a warning sign instead of a deal?
Doll factories set minimum pricing for their authorised resellers, so genuine vendors have very little room to discount — usually 10–15% below list. A shop advertising 50% or 70% off is therefore either not selling the doll it claims to be selling, or not selling a doll at all.
This is counterintuitive, which is exactly why it works so well as a filter: the offer that looks best is the one most likely to take your money.
How much does a sex doll actually cost in the first year?
Budget 15–25% above the sticker price. Typical list prices are $800–$1,800 for full-size TPE, $1,800–$3,500 for full-size platinum silicone, and $150–$700 for a torso. On top of that:
Factory add-ons — standing feet, upgraded skeleton, implanted hair — commonly $150–$400.
First-year care supplies — about $140 for TPE (cleaner, powder, mineral oil, repair kit) or $60 for silicone.
Storage — $30 for an under-bed box, around $120 for a proper closet setup, several hundred for a flight case.
Import charges — since 2025 these apply to US shipments at any value.
Storage is the line buyers forget most often, and a standard closet rod will not hold a full-size doll. The True Cost Calculator puts your own numbers through this.
Do I have to pay customs duty on a doll imported into the United States?
Yes — and the widespread advice that shipments under $800 arrive duty-free is out of date.
The US de minimis exemption was suspended for all countries on 29 August 2025 under Executive Order 14324, and interim final rules in June 2026 suspended it indefinitely for merchandise arriving by every mode other than the international postal network. A doll shipped to a US buyer now requires a customs entry regardless of value, and will usually also pick up a carrier brokerage or disbursement fee.
What nobody can honestly give you is a duty rate : the tariff classification for full-size dolls is genuinely unsettled, so any specific percentage you read is a guess presented as a fact. Ask the vendor whether the price is DDP (duties already paid) or DDU (you settle on arrival). The full breakdown is here .
Is it legal to buy and import an adult doll?
For adult-form dolls it is legal for private adult buyers in most Western markets — the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Germany, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea and Singapore among them — though tax treatment differs in each. Some jurisdictions should be treated as prohibited; Malaysia and Thailand are in that group.
Every jurisdiction we examined prohibits dolls with a childlike appearance, and in several of them importing one is a criminal offence rather than a customs matter. Rules for eleven destinations are listed here. This is general information, not legal advice — verify your own country's current position before ordering.
Should I choose TPE or silicone?
One question settles it: will you genuinely keep up a monthly maintenance routine?
If yes, TPE gives you a softer feel for several hundred dollars less. If you are honest with yourself and the answer is no, choose platinum silicone or wait until you can afford it. TPE is porous, cannot be fully sterilised, and degrades if it is not cleaned, dried, powdered and periodically oiled. Silicone is non-porous, holds fine detail for years, needs only occasional washing and powdering, and lasts longest. A silicone head on a TPE body is a genuine middle path that most factories offer. Full comparison.
How heavy is a full-size doll, and does the material change it?
A full-size doll weighs 55–100+ lb , and it is limp dead weight that cannot help you carry it. Material barely matters — silicone is marginally denser, but neither material solves a weight problem. Size does: compact builds of roughly 140–155 cm keep weight near 50–60 lb, and most torsos run 13–30 lb, though large 140 cm-class torsos reach 60+ lb.
Weight is the single most common source of post-purchase regret, and almost no shop displays it prominently, because it is one of the few facts likely to stop a sale. We collected the real numbers from 33 listings — height barely predicts weight; build does. The 60-Second Finder asks about it before it asks about anything else.
Is the delivery discreet, and what shows on my card statement?
Reputable vendors ship in a plain brown crate with no product names, branding or images, and a neutral company name on the label. A full-size doll arrives in a box roughly five feet long weighing 60–120 lb, so neighbours will see a large box and nothing more; torsos ship in ordinary parcel boxes.
Billing descriptors are set by the vendor, not by the industry — so ask support in writing what descriptor will appear before you order, and keep the reply. A legitimate shop answers directly. Paying via PayPal adds a layer, since the statement shows PayPal plus a neutral merchant name, and it gives you the 180-day dispute window. More on shipping and privacy.
What are factory photos and why do they matter so much?
Factory photos are pictures of your specific doll — face, body, skin tone, chosen options — taken at the factory before dispatch and sent to you for approval, with the vendor shipping only after you approve.
This single habit prevents the most common complaint in the entire category: a doll that arrives looking nothing like the listing. Approving the photos is your last easy exit from the transaction, so compare them against your order sheet carefully. A vendor who will not put a factory-photo policy in writing before you pay is telling you something important.
How long does an order take to arrive?
Two to eight weeks in total: one to four weeks of production, since these are made to order, then factory photos and your approval, then one to three weeks of freight and local delivery. Silence during production is normal, and tracking commonly stalls for several days at customs.
A shop claiming everything is in stock and ships today at factory prices is describing drop-shipping rather than manufacturing — a warning sign rather than good service.
What do I do if the doll arrives damaged or is not what I ordered?
Film the unboxing continuously, from sealed crate to unwrapped doll, before you open anything. That video is the evidence that wins disputes.
Note visible crate damage with the courier at delivery if you can.
Document everything in photographs and contact the vendor in writing immediately.
Use your real leverage: a PayPal dispute or a credit card chargeback — both fit "goods significantly not as described". Which one is stronger is not obvious, and it is worth knowing before you choose: in the UK a credit card can additionally carry a statutory Section 75 claim against the issuer, while paying through an intermediary may break the chain that claim depends on. Check what covers your order .
Never accept a partial refund in exchange for changing a negative review. That trade removes your leverage, and it is common enough in this category to have a name: review extortion.
Should a first-time buyer start with a torso?
Often, yes. A torso is a partial body typically weighing 13–30 lb — drawer-storable, $150–$700 — roughly a fifth of a full-size doll on price, weight and storage burden.
If your honest answers about lifting, space or budget suggest a full-size doll would become a burden, a torso is the cheapest way to find out whether you enjoy ownership at all before committing four figures. Buyers who start small and upgrade later rarely regret it; buyers who start large and find it unmanageable regret it often. The full comparison, including what a torso genuinely gives up.
What maintenance does a doll actually need?
TPE: clean with mild soap and warm water after each use, then dry thoroughly — budget 15–30 minutes for that, every time — that is the step people skip and the reason mould happens. Dust with pure cornstarch monthly to stop the surface going tacky. Apply a light coat of mineral oil every one to three months to prevent drying cracks. Keep it away from heat and from dark clothing, since dye transfer is the most common cosmetic damage and is hard to reverse.
Silicone: clean after use, powder occasionally, no oiling. Water-based lubricant only — silicone-based lubricant degrades silicone skin. The full routine.
How does DollScout make money, and does that change the recommendations?
Through disclosed affiliate commission from vendors that pass our published vetting criteria, plus Amazon Associates commission on accessory links. It never costs you more.
There are no paid placements and no sponsored reviews, and a vendor that fails vetting stays failed at any commission rate. The criteria are published in full , the same ten-point checklist is given away free so you can replace us entirely, and the printable checklist deliberately carries no affiliate links at all. We currently list one vetted vendor rather than a ranked field, because vetting is expensive and the list grows at the speed we can verify rather than the speed we can monetise.
One nobody asks until it is late: how do you get rid of one? The four routes out — and why dumping it is the specific act that keeps triggering police investigations. Didn't find your question? The four free tools cover the decisions behind most of them: Scam-Check for the shop, 60-Second Finder for the product, True Cost Calculator for the budget, and the printable checklist for the whole purchase.

For people who review dolls on YouTube, answer questions on forums, or moderate the places buyers actually ask. Everything below is free to quote, embed, screenshot or rewrite — including commercially.
Every figure on this site is free to quote, embed or rewrite, commercial
use included, with no attribution required. The raw dataset is CC BY 4.0 as
JSON and CSV, with its limitations stated next to it. None of the
copy-paste snippets below contains an affiliate link, so using one cannot
quietly monetise your audience.
The deal, stated plainly: we are a new site with data nobody else publishes, and no audience. You have an audience and get asked the same three questions every week — is this shop legit, how heavy is it, what will customs cost. We would rather you use our answers than write them again from scratch.
None of the snippets on this page contain an affiliate link , and none of them require credit. That is deliberate: a snippet that quietly monetises your audience is one you would be right to refuse.
What facts can you quote from this site?
Everything here is checkable. If you find one of these wrong, tell us and we will correct it publicly .
Height barely predicts weight — build does. Across 33 current listings we recorded, 150–151 cm dolls ran from 43 lb (slim B-cup) to 94 lb (heavy M-cup), and a slim 151 cm doll was lighter than every 140 cm doll in the sample. Full chart and method →
"Torso" hides a five-fold range. Small torsos from 13 lb; large 140 cm-class torsos 62–65 lb — as heavy as some complete dolls.
The US $800 duty-free allowance is gone. Suspended for all countries on 29 August 2025 (EO 14324), made indefinite for non-postal shipments in June 2026. Germany dropped its €150 threshold on 1 July 2026. Sources →
Nobody can honestly quote a US duty rate for a full-size doll. The tariff classification is unsettled. The useful question is DDP or DDU.
A 50%+ discount is a counterfeit signal, not a bargain. Factories set minimum pricing; legitimate vendors sit roughly 10–15% below list.
Routine care costs 15–30 minutes after every use , before any monthly work. That number, not the word "maintenance", is what decides TPE vs silicone.
The TPE-vs-silicone hygiene difference has a measured number. In the one published study we could find (2014, n=12, vibrators not dolls), HPV DNA was still detectable on a thermoplastic-elastomer surface 24 hours after cleaning with a commercial cleaner in 40% of positive samples — and on silicone in none. Limits and source on the page; it matters for shared and second-hand use, not solo. Study, limits and what it changes →
A credit-card deposit protects the whole price, not the deposit. UK s.75 runs on the item's cash price (over £100, up to £30,000), so a £300 deposit on a £1,800 made-to-order doll is covered for the doll — read directly from the statute and the Financial Ombudsman, not from forum advice. The checker →
Where do you get the raw data?
Every figure above is computed from a dataset we publish in full — 42 listings as JSON and CSV under CC BY 4.0. Rebuild our charts, correct them, or use the rows in your own video. No permission needed, no affiliate links in it.
Copy-paste snippets
YouTube description
Before you buy from anyone — three free tools, no signup, no affiliate links in them:
• Is the shop legit? 10-point check: https://thedollscout.com/scam-check
• What will it actually weigh? Real data from 33 listings: https://thedollscout.com/guides/height-weight
• What will it really cost? Duty, care, storage: https://thedollscout.com/cost-calculator
(Not sponsored, not affiliated with me — just the clearest versions of these I've found.)
Click to select. Drop the last line if it doesn't fit your channel's voice.
Forum reply — "is this site legit?"
Run it through this before you pay anything: https://thedollscout.com/scam-check
Short version of what it checks: pricing within ~10-15% of factory list (a 50%+ discount is a counterfeit signal, not a deal), PayPal or card accepted, a written factory-photo-before-dispatch policy, and brand authorisation the factory itself will confirm.
Also worth asking before you pay: which country does it physically ship from, and is the price DDP or DDU. Both catch problems that don't show up on the product page.
No link required — the four checks work on their own if you'd rather not link out.
Forum reply — "how heavy is it?"
Don't guess from the height — it barely predicts weight. In 33 real listings, 150-151cm dolls ranged from 43lb (slim build) to 94lb (heavy build). A slim 151cm doll was lighter than every 140cm doll in the sample.
Take the stated weight of the exact doll you're looking at and carry that up your stairs before you buy. It'll be harder than the test, because a doll is limp and can't hold on.
Full chart: https://thedollscout.com/guides/height-weight
Short / Discord / chat
Free 10-point scam check before you pay any doll shop: https://thedollscout.com/scam-check — no signup, no affiliate links. The counterintuitive one: a 50%+ discount IS the scam signal.
Embed the checklist
The first-time buyer checklist is free, ungated, and has no affiliate links on the printable version — so it is safe to hand to your audience. Paste this anywhere:
<p><strong>Before you pay any doll shop:</strong> a free printable pre-purchase checklist —
weight test, all-in budget, vetting the shop, the factory-photo rule, arrival-day checks.
No email required: <a href="https://thedollscout.com/checklist">thedollscout.com/checklist</a></p>
What do we ask for in return?
We don't ask for credit. Use the facts uncredited if that suits you better. We would rather the information circulate than be attributed.
We don't ask for a link. If one is useful to your audience, great. If not, the snippets stand alone on purpose.
Please don't spam with these. Dropping the same link into unrelated threads gets you banned and gets this domain blacklisted — which destroys the only thing we have. Use them where someone actually asked.
Tell us when we're wrong. Corrections get published with the date. That standard is the only reason any of this is worth quoting.
Full disclosure, since you'd be vouching for us: DollScout earns affiliate commission on some outbound links elsewhere on this site, and we publish the criticism of the one vendor we earn from , including the parts that fail our own criteria. None of that money touches the pages linked from this one. If you're going to cite us to your audience, read how we work first and decide for yourself.

## MCP Endpoint: Call These Tools From Your AI Assistant
URL: https://thedollscout.com/mcp

Call these tools from your AI assistant
We already publish the data and the rules. This makes them
callable: an assistant can ask with your numbers and get the same answer this
site would give, including the parts we could not verify.
Endpoint: https://thedollscout.com/mcp —
Model Context Protocol over streamable HTTP. No key, no account, no rate limit
worth documenting. Open it in a browser to see the tool list.
The six tools
Tool Answers
doll_weight_by_height What dolls of a given height actually weigh, from recorded listings — the specification listings routinely omit.
payment_recourse Whether UK Section 75 appears to apply and whether a chargeback is available, by payment method and price.
first_year_cost What a doll costs in year one beyond the sticker: import charge, care, storage, repair reserve.
doll_price_bands Recorded floor, median and top — for judging whether an advertised price is plausible.
scam_check_signals The ten checks to run against an unfamiliar shop before entering a card number.
import_rules Legal status, duty and customs for importing into a given country, with that country's sources.
What makes this different from an API over a spreadsheet
No rule is reimplemented in the endpoint. Every answer is
read from the published JSON at request time — the same files behind
the dataset , the
recourse matrix and the cost model . If
those change, the endpoint changes with them, or it stops answering. It cannot
quietly disagree with the pages, because there is no second copy of the rules
to drift.
Every answer carries its caveats. The recording date, the
dataset's stated limitations, the open questions. A tool that returns a bare
number strips exactly the context a careful page spent paragraphs
establishing, and the caller has no way to know what was dropped.
It refuses. Ask about a height we have no listings for and
it says so and lists the heights it does have. Ask about Section 75 outside
the UK and it returns "not verified" — never a clean "no", because that would
be a claim about your country's law that we have not checked.
Adding it to a client
{
"mcpServers": {
"dollscout": {
"type": "http",
"url": "https://thedollscout.com/mcp"
}
}
}
This site earns affiliate commissions from vetted vendors, which
is disclosed on every page that carries such a link. The MCP endpoint
contains no affiliate links and no vendor ranking — it returns
measurements and rules. Data is CC BY 4.0; the
methodology explains how it was collected and what it
does not cover.

## Sex Doll Weight by Height: Real Listings, Sample Sizes Stated
URL: https://thedollscout.com/weight/

What dolls actually weigh, by height
50 listings recorded 2026-08-11 · every number sourced, or marked unverified
Shops routinely print the height and not the weight, so buyers
plan around the one number that does not tell them whether they can move the
thing.
These are measured from live listings, with the sample size shown next to every
range — including the heights where the sample is too small and we say so
instead of writing a page.
Height Listings Weight range Median Spread at one height
150cm 30 57–79 lb 60 lb 22 lb (39%)
160cm 15 79–94 lb 85 lb 15 lb (19%)
140cm 4 84–104 lb No page: 4 listings is not enough to state a range we would defend.
165cm 1 79–79 lb No page: 1 listings is not enough to state a range we would defend.
A page exists only where we have 10 or more listings
at that height. The rest are shown with their real counts and no
page — generating one per height regardless is how a site ends up
publishing "typical weight" figures with nothing behind them, which is the
practice this site exists to argue against.
Download the dataset (CC BY 4.0) ·
the full weight chart and method .

## How Much Does a 150cm Sex Doll Weigh? 30 Real Listings
URL: https://thedollscout.com/weight/150cm

Weight by height / 150cm
How much does a 150cm doll weigh?
30 listings recorded 2026-08-11 · every number sourced, or marked unverified
57–79 lb (26–36 kg), median 60 lb. That is a 22 lb spread — 39% — between the lightest and heaviest doll at one identical height, because build, not height, drives weight. It is a sample of one catalogue on one date, not a market survey.
Why two 150cm dolls differ by 22 lb
Height is the number every shop prints and it is the wrong one to plan
around. Across these 30 listings at exactly 150 cm, the heaviest is
39% heavier than the lightest. Build — cup size, hip volume, whether
the bust is solid or gel — decides both the mass and how much material the
factory uses, which is why it moves the price too: these same listings run $899 to $2,866.
This matters before you buy, not after. Weight is the most reported source
of first-buyer regret, and it is the specification shops are least likely to
print next to the photo.

What to do with the number
Plan storage before you order. A closet rod is not rated
for 60 lb of dead weight. The True Cost
Calculator puts a real storage figure into your first-year total.

the honest trade-off is mostly
about weight.
